title: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH
summary: The installer currently completes while the launcher directory never reaches PATH in a freshly opened terminal. It picks the profile file from $SHELL alone: on macOS a bash login shell never reads ~/.bashrc, and under `curl … | sh` $SHELL can be empty, sending the block to ~/.profile while the terminal reads ~/.zshrc. It also never checks that its own change took effect. This change makes the installer detect the real login shell, write the block into a profile file a new terminal actually reads, start a clean login shell afterwards and verify that `forgel-code` resolves, and fail with a message naming the edited file and the observed PATH when it does not. --uninstall removes the block from every profile file the installer can have written.
requirements: install.sh must not derive the profile file from $SHELL alone: when $SHELL is unset, empty or names an unhandled shell, it reads the account login shell (macOS `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell`, otherwise the passwd entry) and only then falls back to $HOME/.profile.
For zsh the block goes into $HOME/.zshrc, created when missing.

For bash the block goes into the first existing file of $HOME/.bash_profile, $HOME/.bash_login, $HOME/.profile; if none exists, $HOME/.bash_profile is created. The block is never written to $HOME/.bashrc alone, because a login bash shell does not read it.

FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE still overrides the chosen file; FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH and FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT still leave every profile file untouched, print the exact `export PATH="<bin>:$PATH"` line and exit 0.

After writing the block the installer verifies it: it starts the detected login shell as a login interactive shell in a cleared environment (HOME, SHELL, TERM, minimal PATH) and resolves `command -v forgel-code`; the result must be the launcher just written.

If verification fails, the installer exits non-zero and prints the edited profile file, the block written and the PATH seen in the fresh shell. It must not claim the change is active unless verification passed.
On success the installer prints the detected shell, the profile file written and the fresh-shell check result.
Re-running keeps exactly one marked block per edited file and leaves the rest of the file byte-identical.

--uninstall removes the marked block from every profile file this installer can have written (.zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile), leaves the rest of each file unchanged, and still removes the prefix and the launcher.
The documented `curl … | sh` shape keeps working: POSIX sh, passes `sh -n`, uses `set -eu`, never reads stdin.
README documents which file is edited per shell, that the installer verifies the result in a fresh shell, how the opt-out line is printed, and what --uninstall removes.
acceptance: With SHELL unset and a zsh login shell the block lands in $HOME/.zshrc and a fresh `env -i` zsh resolves forgel-code to the installed launcher.
With SHELL=/bin/bash and an existing ~/.bash_profile the block lands there and ~/.bashrc is neither created nor modified.
With SHELL=/bin/bash and no bash profile file the installer creates ~/.bash_profile with the block.
When the edited file is not read by the detected shell (for example FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE points at an ignored file) the installer exits non-zero and the message names that file.
With FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 no profile file in the temporary HOME is created or modified, the export line is printed, the exit code is 0.
Running the installer twice leaves exactly one marked block and identical content.
--uninstall removes the block from every candidate file holding it and leaves unrelated lines unchanged.
A piped `sh` install with the script on stdin still installs and verifies.
constraints: Keep the script POSIX sh and safe to pipe into a shell; no bashisms, no stdin reads.
Do not change the client package, the entry point, the build backend or the launcher format beyond what the PATH fix needs.
Do not weaken existing installer tests; extend them.
Tests must not need network, the real GitHub repository or the real user profile: temporary HOME and local source tree only.
assumptions: The fix belongs to the `code` repository, which holds install.sh, the launcher and the installer tests.
The earlier install run used the opt-out switch, so no profile was edited at all; that path works as designed and the change focuses on the silent-ineffective-profile case.
The default tag v0.1.0 stays; the release is published after this change is accepted so the tag contains the fixed script.

external_dependencies.name: macOS Directory Service command `dscl`
external_dependencies.interface: Used only for macOS login-shell detection: `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` prints `UserShell: <path>`. A test stub is placed first on PATH so macOS behavior is deterministic on Linux.
external_dependencies.evidence: `install.sh` requires the macOS lookup `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell`; the repository Linux environment does not provide `dscl`, so tests need a deterministic stand-in.
external_dependencies.stub:
#!/bin/sh
# Deterministic test stub for the macOS Directory Service call:
#   dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell
# The shell is selected by FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL (default /bin/zsh).
if [ "$#" -ne 4 ] || [ "$1" != "." ] || [ "$2" != "-read" ] || [ "$4" != "UserShell" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' 'dscl stub: supports only: dscl . -read <home> UserShell' >&2
    exit 64
fi
shell=${FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL:-/bin/zsh}
printf 'UserShell: %s\n' "$shell"

external_dependencies.name: passwd database (getent / /etc/passwd)
external_dependencies.interface: Fallback login-shell lookup: `getent passwd "$(id -u)" | cut -d: -f7`, with an `/etc/passwd` fallback such as `awk -F: -v u="$(id -u)" '$3 == u { print $7 }' /etc/passwd`. Tests may inject a fake `getent` first on PATH for controlled output.
external_dependencies.evidence: The environment is a Linux base with the account database available locally; `install.sh` uses the account login shell when `$SHELL` is unset, empty or unhandled.

external_dependencies.name: zsh
external_dependencies.interface: Verification shell: `env -i HOME="$HOME" SHELL=/bin/zsh TERM=dumb PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" /bin/zsh -l -i -c 'command -v forgel-code'`. Profile writes target `$HOME/.zshrc` for zsh.
external_dependencies.evidence: The environment contract provides zsh, and the required fresh-shell test invokes zsh as a login interactive shell under `env -i` to resolve `forgel-code` from the written `.zshrc`.

external_dependencies.name: bash
external_dependencies.interface: Verification shell: `env -i HOME="$HOME" SHELL=/bin/bash TERM=dumb PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" /bin/bash -l -i -c 'command -v forgel-code'`. Login profile writes target the first existing of `$HOME/.bash_profile`, `$HOME/.bash_login`, `$HOME/.profile`, creating `.bash_profile` when none exists.
external_dependencies.evidence: Bash is provided by the environment and is required by the fresh-shell verification and login-profile behavior described in the task.

result.summary: Reworked install.sh so the PATH block lands in the profile the login shell actually reads and is proven active in a fresh shell; documented the behaviour in README.md and covered it in tests/test_install.py. install.sh now: (1) keeps the FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE override first; (2) detects the login shell from $SHELL only when that names a shell the installer handles, otherwise from the account login shell (dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell, then getent passwd / /etc/passwd), falling back to /bin/sh; (3) picks ~/.zshrc for zsh, the first existing of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile for bash (creating ~/.bash_profile) and never ~/.bashrc alone, ~/.profile otherwise, creating the file when missing; (4) writes the single marked block with the unchanged markers and the exact export PATH="<bin>:$PATH" line; (5) verifies by starting the detected shell with env -i (HOME, SHELL, TERM, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin) as `-l -i` and requiring `command -v forgel-code` to equal the launcher just written; on failure it exits non-zero and prints the login shell, the edited profile file, the block written, the fresh PATH and the resolved path; on success it prints the detected shell, the profile file and the fresh-shell result; (6) --uninstall removes the marked block from .zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .bash_profile, .bash_login and .profile plus the prefix and launcher, leaving the rest of each file unchanged. The opt-out variables still leave every profile untouched, print the exact export line and exit 0, and a piped `sh` install still works (the script never reads stdin). README now documents the per-shell profile table, the account-login-shell fallback, the fresh-shell verification and its failure report, the exact opt-out line and what --uninstall removes. Added tests: shell detection from the account login shell through the recorded dscl stub with a fresh `env -i` zsh resolving the launcher, bash profile placement with and without an existing ~/.bash_profile (and no ~/.bashrc), installer reporting of shell/profile/fresh-check, non-zero exit naming the edited file when the shell ignores it, and --uninstall clearing the block from every candidate file. Verified with `python -m unittest tests.test_install -v` (23 tests OK), `python -m unittest tests.test_readme_install -v` (26 tests OK, including the `sh -n install.sh` guard) and the full suite `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (171 tests OK).
assumptions: The fix belongs to the `code` repository, which holds install.sh, the launcher and the installer tests.
The earlier install run used the opt-out switch, so no profile was edited at all; that path works as designed and the change focuses on the silent-ineffective-profile case.
The default tag v0.1.0 stays; the release is published after this change is accepted so the tag contains the fixed script.

$SHELL counts as unusable when it is empty or names a shell the installer does not handle; because a POSIX shell re-exports SHELL from the passwd entry, the detection tests set SHELL to the empty string to exercise the account login-shell lookup, which behaves exactly like an unset value inside the script.
The account login-shell lookup tries `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` whenever dscl is on PATH (the recorded stub interface), then getent/passwd, then falls back to /bin/sh, which reads ~/.profile.

Verification runs only the real `-l -i` startup of the detected shell under `env -i`; when that shell's login mode reads no file (a POSIX sh with no login file), the block is unverifiable, so the installer fails and names the file rather than reporting a false success.
The --uninstall candidate list is exactly .zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .bash_profile, .bash_login and .profile, matching the recorded assumption.
README's opt-out example uses the default $HOME/.local/bin so the shown line is character-identical to what the installer prints for a default install.
No CHANGELOG entry was added because the specification lists only install.sh, tests/test_install.py and README.md as affected files and no decision changed.

checks.criterion: With SHELL unset and a zsh login shell the block lands in $HOME/.zshrc and a fresh `env -i` zsh resolves forgel-code to the installed launcher.

review.summary: The attributed change implements the specification in install.sh: profile selection now goes through a detected login shell ($SHELL first when handled, then the account login shell from dscl/getent/passwd, then /bin/sh), zsh writes to ~/.zshrc, bash writes to the first existing of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile and creates ~/.bash_profile when none exists, ~/.bashrc is no longer used, the override and both opt-outs keep working (printing the exact `export PATH="<bin>:$PATH"` line and exiting 0), and after writing the block the installer starts the detected shell as `env -i ... -l -i -c` and only reports success when `command -v forgel-code` resolves to the launcher it just wrote; a failed check prints the login shell, profile file, block and the PATH the fresh shell saw and exits non-zero. --uninstall now strips the marked block from the six candidate profile files while leaving the rest untouched, re-runs stay idempotent, the script remains POSIX sh with `set -eu` and never reads stdin (the fresh shell is given </dev/null), and README documents the per-shell file, the fresh-shell verification, the opt-out line and what uninstall removes without adding a second install path. The dscl stub in tests matches the recorded external-dependency evidence exactly, and passwd/zsh/bash are used as direct interfaces. The attributed file tests/test_diag_tmp.py is not present in the current tree and no test removals were detected, so nothing is missing there. QA's gate (full suite, sh -n, the fresh-shell acceptance case, environment checks) passed, and I found no requirement violation, no unrequested feature, no weakened test, and no security issue in the attributed diff.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: profile selection does not rely on $SHELL alone; an unusable $SHELL falls back to the account login shell (macOS dscl, otherwise passwd) and only then to ~/.profile
requirements.note: detect_login_shell uses $SHELL when handled, then account_login_shell (dscl, getent, /etc/passwd awk), then /bin/sh whose family maps to ~/.profile.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: for zsh the block goes into $HOME/.zshrc, created when missing
requirements.note: profile_path zsh branch prints $HOME_DIR/.zshrc and add_profile_block creates the file.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: for bash the block goes into the first existing of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile, creating ~/.bash_profile when none exists, never into ~/.bashrc alone
requirements.note: bash branch loops over the three names in order and defaults to ~/.bash_profile; .bashrc no longer appears in profile_path.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE overrides the chosen file; FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH and FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT leave every profile untouched, print the exact export line and exit 0
requirements.note: profile_path returns the override first; add_path's opt-out branch prints `export PATH="<bin>:$PATH"` and returns 0 before any detection or write.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: after writing, the installer starts the detected login shell as a login interactive shell in a cleared environment and requires command -v forgel-code to resolve to the launcher just written
requirements.note: verify_profile runs `env -i HOME=... SHELL=... TERM=dumb PATH=/usr/bin:/bin $shell -l -i -c ...` and compares the resolved path to $LAUNCHER; no stub or re-implementation of profile loading.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: a failed verification exits non-zero and prints the edited profile file, the block written and the PATH seen in the fresh shell, and does not claim the change is active
requirements.note: verification_failure prints the shell, profile file, the marker block, the fresh PATH and the resolved path, returns 1, and add_path propagates failure so the success message is never emitted.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: on success the installer prints the detected shell, the profile file written and the fresh-shell check result
requirements.note: The success branch prints login shell, profile path and `command -v forgel-code -> $VERIFIED_PATH`.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: re-running keeps exactly one marked block per edited file and leaves the rest of the file byte-identical
requirements.note: add_profile_block removes any existing block before appending, and the trailing-newline guard is stable across runs, so the remainder is unchanged and one block remains.

requirements.requirement: FR-9: --uninstall removes the block from every candidate file (.zshrc, .zprofile, .zshenv, .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile), leaves the rest unchanged, and still removes the prefix and launcher
requirements.note: The uninstall loop iterates PROFILE_NAMES and calls remove_profile_block, which uses awk to drop only the marked block; prefix and launcher removal is unchanged.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: the curl | sh shape keeps working: POSIX sh, sh -n clean, set -eu, never reads stdin
requirements.note: `set -eu` remains at the top, no bashisms, and the fresh shell is started with `</dev/null` so it cannot consume the piped script; QA's `sh -n install.sh` and piped-install checks passed.

requirements.requirement: FR-11: README documents the file per shell, the fresh-shell verification, the printed opt-out line and what --uninstall removes
requirements.note: README adds the per-shell table, detection/verification paragraphs, the printed export line and the uninstall candidate list.

requirements.requirement: Technical: markers and block content unchanged, block is the exact export line matching the opt-out output
requirements.note: MARKER_START/MARKER_END are byte-identical to before and both write and opt-out paths use the same printf of `export PATH="$BIN_DIR:$PATH"`.

requirements.requirement: Technical: existing tests keep passing and no test is weakened; no unjustified test removal
requirements.note: No test removals were detected; the suite gained constants (CANDIDATE_PROFILES, DSCL_STUB) and the full suite plus the acceptance cases pass under QA.

requirements.requirement: External dependencies: dscl stub matches the recorded evidence; passwd, zsh and bash used as direct interfaces
requirements.note: DSCL_STUB reproduces the recorded stub verbatim (4-arg check, FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL, `UserShell: %s`); the installer reads passwd via getent/awk and starts the real zsh/bash binaries.

requirements.requirement: Non-goals respected: no change to install location, launcher format, FORGEL_CODE_HOME/BIN defaults, options, README install path, tag pinning or the test_readme_install policy
requirements.note: Only profile selection, verification, uninstall cleanup and their documentation changed; the pip invoke call was reflowed, not altered, and the README one-command block remains first and unchanged.
QA reported pass for the fresh-shell zsh case, `sh -n install.sh`, the full test suite and both environment checks; no failing acceptance check was recorded.

requirements.requirement: Committed artifacts are English and the commit uses the imperative mood with git commit -s
requirements.note: README and test names are English; the commit message is imperative and carries a Signed-off-by line, without a tool name attribution line.
